sampling_model.design: Dominated i.i.d. observed data on the canonical full ball \(\mathcal V_P=\{P':\|dP'/dP-1\|_\infty<\varepsilon\}\), intersected with the full transported fixed-nullity, fixed-cokernel, reduced-modulus-separated stratum and both bridge-solvability loci. Every DQM curve remaining in this set is admitted; tangent richness is not defined into the model.
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment is binary. The statistical target is the observed joint-bridge functional; equality with the ATE uses only the separately stated latent consistency, exchangeability, positivity, negative-control, and bridge-compatibility assumptions.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment-bridge existence is an observed solvability restriction. No injectivity, surjectivity, preferred minimum-norm bridge, or bridge uniqueness is imposed on the main model.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fold-indexed ridge/Galerkin affine ensemble remains an explicit proposed estimator. Its deterministic four-corner conversion and mixed-bias algebra are valid, but the current primitive conditions do not yet prove learned projection convergence because multiplier, dimension, training-dependence, and Gram-null-space controls are incomplete.

body.tldr: The model is repaired to use the full local \(L^\infty\) likelihood-ratio ball and the full fixed-defect, spectrally separated operator stratum, admitting every DQM curve that remains in the joint outcome- and treatment-solvability intersection. Reverse score lifting on this saturated general germ remains open and is not inferred from pointwise operator perturbation. The affine score identity and kernel perturbation lemma are proved. The positive \(36\)-cell witness is independently reproduced, with \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}=773723312/334026875\) and strict single-pair nonattainment; singular \(3\)-by-\(3\) and transverse \(4\)-by-\(4\) tests also yield the proposed annihilator. The outcome-only comparison is repaired by defining a smooth gauge-selected parameter, giving \(V_{\mathrm{out}}=30544/13125\) and gap \(2166784/200416125\). General learned-projection efficiency and Wald inference remain open because their primitive rate proof is incomplete. The observed bridge functional has a causal ATE interpretation only under the separate latent identification proposition.

project_justification.gap: Existing nonunique-bridge work supplies valid regular inference under additional selection and regularity conditions, but the full tangent closure of the simultaneous outcome- and treatment-solvability germ is not established. A base-law treatment bridge also does not, by itself, define an outcome-only neighboring-law parameter.
project_justification.niche: The proposed contribution concerns the quotient tangent geometry of a saturated fixed-defect observed-law model, where both bridge fibers may be non-singleton and treatment-solvability normals can reduce variance beyond a well-defined outcome-only selected-parameter comparator.
project_justification.fill: This round proves the affine normal identity, operator-kernel stability, exact finite tangent and nonattainment witnesses, and the corrected outcome-only projection gap. It leaves the general score-lifting theorem and primitive learned-projection inference theorem explicit as the two load-bearing unresolved steps.

body.related_work: ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness and BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified motivate regular selected-pair inference, but this round does not identify their selected limits with the displayed finite pair; those comparisons are therefore informative rather than theorem-level dominance claims. ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification motivates outcome-only overidentification, but its exact neighboring-law parameter was not imported. The proved replacement is an explicit positive finite fixed-rank comparator with a gauge-selected smooth bridge functional. CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal remains the unique-and-surjective endpoint, now separated into an algebraic general reduction and an unconditional positive finite full-rank corollary. SeveriniTripathi2012EfficiencyBounds is prior art for quotient-functional projection, while AiChen2012SequentialMoments, AiShan2025EfficientProximalATE, and BennettEtAl2023SourceConditionDR inform but do not prove the unresolved learned affine projection.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The main unresolved mathematical step is reverse lifting on the saturated infinite-dimensional intersection. Continuous kernel projections do not provide differentiable bridge selections or actual path realization. Separate second moments do not control all products needed for bridge-score differentiation. The learned dictionary theorem additionally lacks dimension-aware multiplier bounds, valid concentration for dictionaries fitted on the same training observations, and control of ridge amplification in population Gram null directions. Closed range excludes generic compact infinite-rank inverse problems. Rank-changing neighborhoods, general direct-integral measurable charts, and a SUPPORT reanalysis remain outside scope. The final Bennett publisher text was not verified here, so no claim depends on its exact theorem wording.
body.honest_scope: Unconditional results are the algebraic affine identity, operator perturbation, the positive finite regular witness, the singular branch witness, the transverse four-level witness, the corrected selected-score gap, and the explicit outcome-only selected-parameter projection gap. The general quotient efficiency theorem remains conditional on score lifting and pathwise score validity. The general learned-projection and Wald theorems remain open. The main target is an observed bridge functional and becomes a causal ATE only through the separate identification proposition. No efficiency claim is made for arbitrary path-poor subcharts, rank-changing unions, generic compact ill-posed operators, or a published outcome-only model not explicitly imported.
body.interpretation: For redundant proxies, a chosen bridge pair can yield a valid score yet fail to minimize variance across the affine score hull. The exact witness proves that this is not merely a numerical optimization artifact. A SUPPORT analysis could use the factorization residual and finite normal projection as diagnostics, but no claim is made that the published specification has the witness's rank deficiency or that its estimator selects the displayed pair.
